name: Laudspeaker
founder_evidence: Abheek Basu previously worked in product management and software engineering, including product/business development at Orbital Insight, and holds Penn engineering and Wharton business degrees.
Mahamad Charawi previously worked as a senior software engineer at Cisco, co-founded CameraOpus, and holds Penn engineering and Wharton business degrees.

name: FlightCar
outcome: shut down (2016); technology sold to Mercedes-Benz
founder_evidence: Rujul Zaparde deferred Harvard to build FlightCar after co-founding the nonprofit Drinking Water for India; the service launched in February 2013, after the W13 application period.
Kevin Petrovic deferred Princeton, previously operated a profitable resale business, and co-founded Drinking Water for India.
Shri Ganeshram, an additional documented co-founder and CTO, programmed from childhood and left MIT to build FlightCar.

name: Qvin
founder_evidence: Sara Naseri began menstrual-blood research in medical school at Aarhus, later researched at Stanford, and studied microfluidic fabrication at Harvard; Qvin pivoted from in-pad analysis to laboratory analysis during YC in 2016.

Søren Therkelsen studied IT at IT University of Copenhagen and microfluidic fabrication at Harvard, previously co-founded SCALEit, and led Qvin product and operations; Qvin participated in the funded YC Fellowship in 2015 before W16.

name: Spaces Life
outcome: shut down (year unknown; YC entity inactive)
founder_evidence: Shazz Bhunnoo started the underlying Spaces rental-property operation in London in 2006, before YC, and describes subsequent shifts between property operations and scalable property-management technology.
Mike Laming is a University of Kent alumnus and technologist whom YC identifies as a Spaces Life co-founder; detailed pre-founding employment was not established.

name: Ditto
founder_evidence: Jo Ma, also known as Jolena Ma, attended Stanford and previously worked at Asana, IDEO CoLab, Crunchbase and Instagram; she leads Ditto's go-to-market organization.
Jessica Ouyang attended Stanford and previously worked at Google, Twitter, Lightstep and IDEO, with additional university medical/scientific research affiliations listed by YC.

name: Wave
founder_evidence: Drew Durbin graduated from Brown, built social enterprises in Africa and co-founded Sendwave before Wave; the W12 affiliation belongs to the earlier company lineage, whereas Wave launched in Senegal in 2018 and Sendwave's exit completed in 2021.

Lincoln Quirk, an additional co-founder explicitly identified in Wave's founder account, met Durbin at Brown, co-founded Sendwave and built its software while Durbin handled licensing, business development and fundraising.

name: Ready For Zero
outcome: acquired by Avant (2015); product shut down (2016)
founder_evidence: Rod Ebrahimi founded an ISP in high school, studied cognitive science and human-computer interaction, and led Membase's first product launch as its first non-founder employee; his YC bio also lists UCSD and MIT.
Ignacio Thayer worked on statistical machine translation for six years at USC and Google before co-founding ReadyForZero; the founders explicitly described themselves as newcomers to finance.

name: Waydev
founder_evidence: Alex Circei studied business management at Romanian-American University and previously founded Billme, liveMag.ro and StoreBeez; he says Waydev was launched in 2017, had paying customers before W21 and took no institutional capital except YC.
Valentin Buzea, an additional documented co-founder and CTO, attended Politehnica University of Bucharest and previously worked on Homes.forsale, Propsee and other software businesses.

name: Amulyte
founder_evidence: Perry Haldenby attended Waterloo and worked in technology at CGI and TD; later biographies identify him as CTO of Bunz and Blimp Homes after co-founding Amulyte.

Jaclyn Konzelmann earned a Waterloo mechatronics engineering degree, worked at Microsoft from 2010 to 2012, had a patient-care automation engineering placement, and previously founded Integrated Conveyor Simulation Solutions.

name: Seneca Systems
outcome: acquired by Coinbase (2018; some databases report 2019)
founder_evidence: Nick DeMonner earned a philosophy BA at Santa Clara University and was an early software engineer at Gusto before co-founding Seneca, where he moved from CTO to CEO; Coinbase, Metawork and Motor came later.
